missing: a memoized call that reaches lib_memo's cache from Python, which is where (aggregate sum) folds
section: correction to §9j: caching is listed there as a library that BEATS the plain-Python route, and its Python door does not reach it
detail: (config-memoize (aggregate sum)) folds a ground call's answers into one cached value inside cache_call_store_ground (lib/lib_memo.pl, apply_aggregate_mode/2), so the claim (choices 5) == 18 holds only when the call goes through the cache. It does not from Python: with the definition and the memoize both written by a loaded file, two m.eval calls record no cache hit and no miss where two ! forms in a loaded file record one of each, and is-memoized answers true either way [measured 2026-08-22, ai-tmp/idiomb-memoize-repro.py on p14-twins-idiom-b]. So from Python (choices 5) answers 5, 6 and 7. Folding them with Python's sum() would prove Python's sum rather than the cache, which is the example's subject, so the claim is declined. The twin still performs the example's program and states the half that does hold, that the mode is accepted and readable.

missing: a space HANDLE where a builtin takes its space as an ARGUMENT
section: §9c primitive 2: the space handle wearing Python's container protocols
detail: m.space(name) answers a handle, and the handle does not encode as an atom: m.eval(S['import!'](m.space('&self'), ...)) hands the engine Gnd(<MeTTa>) and it answers 'get-atoms expects a space as its argument' / 'match expects a space as the first argument' / a translation failure for import!. Every context-relative door that IS a method dissolves cleanly (space += a, space[pattern], list(space), space.eval(t), space.fn(n)); what has no method is every builtin whose space is one ARGUMENT among several, so the name is written as the symbol its own door takes. Derived demand from this wave, 33 of the 37 files in libraries/: import! in 30 of them, plus type-cast and get-type-space (he_types, he_atomspace), check-space-provider (conformance), peek-atom and take-atom (thread_linda), and the space inside a STORED equation's body (derived_forms, tabling_space_write, tabling_statistics), where a handle could never go because an equation is data that outlives the process.

missing: a Python evaluation door that reaches lib_memo's dispatch hook
section: correction to §9j: the library catalogue's caching entry
detail: A memoized function is not cached when called through m.eval, and therefore through m.fn, m.one and calling a Defined. Reproduction in ai-tmp/idiomb-memoize-repro.py: with (= (sq $x) (* $x $x)) and !(memoize sq) both written by a loaded file, two calls from Python answer ((cache_hit 0) (cache_miss 0)), an empty get-memoize-stats, while two ! forms in a loaded file answer ((cache_hit 1) (cache_miss 1)); is-memoized answers true in both. lib_tabling does NOT share this: @m.cache on fib(30) costs 82,135 inferences against the .metta original's 84,235, which an untabled fib could not do. Eight files in libraries/ are affected (the seven test_memo_* and memo_spaces); seven of them state claims whose answers are the same cached or not, and test_memo_aggregate's is not, which is its own declined entry. One further observable: memoize recompiles by removing each equation and adding it back, which REVERSES the order two clauses answer in, so test_memo_multi_answer compares a sorted multiset.

missing: a cast door that agrees with the engine's type-cast on an undeclared atom
detail: m.cast(S.B, S.type1) raises CastError, 'B does not admit type type1 in &self: its types are %Undefined%', where the engine answers B: an atom nobody declared has type %Undefined%, which the language's own rule treats as a wildcard matching any requested type (engine/prelude.metta, match-type-or and type-cast-holds). The ledger's design for cast is 'typing.cast plus truth', and the truth it adds here is stricter than the language's. The twin asks type-cast directly, which also keeps the refusal answer (Error 1 BadType) as the ATOM the example claims rather than as an exception.

missing: space.type(atom), the dissolution table's own door for get-type
detail: The dissolution table maps (get-type a) to space.type(atom) and the handle has no such method: MeTTa.type is the class-declaration decorator, so m.type(S.a) raises AttributeError, 'Sym object has no attribute __mro__'. The twin names get-type-space, which also has to name its space. Two neighbours in the same section are absent as well: equation(lhs, rhs) as a two-argument TERM builder (only equation(lhs).to(rhs) ships, and it doubles as the pattern, which is what the twin uses), and typed(x, T) for a (: x T) declaration, which is not exported, so a declaration is written S[':'](x, T).

missing: a space handle from the space a library function ANSWERS
section: §9j: the web datastore IS a space
detail: json-decode, dict-space and file-space! each answer a space by NAME, as Sym('&json-1'), and m.space takes a string, refusing a Sym with 'a space name is a string starting with &'. So every use round-trips through str(): m.space(str(decode(text))). The design point underneath works beautifully once the handle is in hand, and it is what makes these twins short: the decoded object's keys are the heads of its atoms, its lookup is a subscript, an absent key answers no rows, and file-space!'s (line N Text) atoms are queried by line number.

missing: a cardinality door that hands an Error ANSWER over as data
detail: m.one and m.fn take the loud reading of an error answer and raise MettaResultError, which is right for a caller that wanted a value and wrong for a claim ABOUT an error atom. So every such claim goes through m.eval and a one-element unpacking, [caught] = m.eval(...), which is Python's own way of saying exactly one answer is expected. Affected here: he_error's catch results and return-on-error, he_types' (type-cast 1 type1 &self) answering (Error 1 BadType), and tabling_space_write's refused tabling declaration.

missing: a with-block for the stack-depth bound, where m.limits covers inferences and timeout
section: §9b: control and modes, modes are with-blocks
detail: The 70,000-step interpreter exercise states (with-pragma! ((max-stack-depth 1000000)) ...). m.limits(timeout=, inferences=) is the shipped block and has no stack-depth knob, so the pragma is built as the term it is. with-pragma! is not in the lane's dissolution table, so this costs no finding; it is recorded because it is the one mode in this folder that the with-block family does not reach.

missing: the twins lane reading a @m.cache body as a compiled body
section: correction to the lane's own source scan
detail: twin_coverage._defines recognises only a decorator named `define`, so a string constant inside a @m.cache body is refused as MeTTa source text. A cached definition IS a compiled body plus a tabling declaration (space.py _cache_define calls install_define), and the compiled match(...) REQUIRES its space as a string constant: the two-argument form lowers to (context-space), which caching refuses with 'nothing declares it pure'. So a function that reads a space cannot be written with @m.cache under this lane, and tabling_space_write and tabling_statistics use @m.define plus an explicit tabled declaration, which also costs them fn.cache_info(), the Python name for the counters tabling_statistics reads. tabling_fib, whose body names no space, uses @m.cache and is the whole file. The fix is one name in _defines.
